intent: Make AI a constrained collaborator inside the Alloy development loop: express intent, inspect a typed proposal, validate it, examine witnesses, apply an explicit draft edit and explicitly save. AI proposes; existing deterministic language, authorization and persistence boundaries decide what is admissible.

scope.primary: End-user Alloy modeling assistance inside the existing React block/source workbench, backed by Spring/Java17 and sandboxed Alloy/Kodkod/SAT4J.
scope.secondary: A reproducible development/evaluation discipline for the Allow team: specifications and Lean policy first, review council, generated test fixtures and controlled feature promotion.
scope.this_delivery: JSON requirements, Lean finite policy supplement, adversarial council and implementation gameplan only. No provider calls with user/corpus data, production source changes, SQL migration, model purchase, deployment or automatic feature enablement.
excluded: General shell, browser, filesystem or SQL agent

precedence.narrow_amendment: Earlier no-generation rules remain the deployed default. Only after this contract's implementation/release gates and explicit installation enablement may a new ai_generate purpose authorize the closed assistance workflow. Remote generation additionally requires ai_disclose grants. Analyze/retrieve/embed/train/export rights do not imply either grant. No amendment enables remote embeddings, external tracing or visitor training.
precedence.public_corpus: ANONYMOUS still has no private corpus metadata/search/import/train access. This specification does not create a public corpus. A separately licensed/publication-reviewed catalog requires a future contract amendment.
precedence.sql: Every PostgreSQL query, transaction control statement, schema/checkpoint/job/budget migration, test and backup remains routed through SQLeanParser. No framework checkpointer, driver or telemetry library may bypass the gateway.
precedence.style: All production Java/JS/TS callables require Javadoc or corresponding documentation, <=30 physical lines per method/function, encapsulated classes and the existing repository checks. AI output does not bypass these rules. Existing narrower artifact/type/resource bounds take precedence.

capabilities.name: Explain selection
capabilities.behavior: Explain an authorized declaration, formula or exact solver witness. Cite occurrence IDs and deterministic evidence. Label inferred intent separately; unresolved positions are not invented.

capabilities.name: Complete typed slot
capabilities.behavior: Propose a small expression for the selected hole using in-scope declarations, nominal ordered relation types and existing partial constraints. Invalid candidates remain diagnostics, never accepted blocks.

capabilities.name: Create from intent
capabilities.behavior: Offer bounded declarations/predicates and explicit assumptions from user intent. User chooses a proposal; no generation on every keystroke and no silent weakening of requirements.

capabilities.name: Repair with evidence
capabilities.behavior: Propose one minimal repair linked to an exact parser/type diagnostic or bounded counterexample. Show changed facts, multiplicities and commands prominently. A passing run is not proof that the repair matches intent.

capabilities.name: Retrieve a relevant pattern
capabilities.behavior: For an authorized admitted record, show exact structured hierarchy, score components, context compatibility and bounded evidence. No cosine score is an equivalence certificate.

capabilities.name: Explore an alternative
capabilities.behavior: Compare at most three sequentially requested alternatives and their exact diffs. User-requested bounded run/check commands execute only through the existing sandboxed job API; AI cannot invent a successful solver receipt.

architecture.frontend: React retains the source/block editor as the primary surface. A contextual assistant panel exposes Explain, Fill slot, Repair and Ask; shows assumptions, ghost blocks, source diff, evidence and Apply to draft. Save remains a separate existing user action. Keyboard actions, focus restoration and screen-reader announcements match pointer affordances.
architecture.authority: Spring resolves the existing bearer to immutable owner/workspace/incarnation on every create/get/cancel/approve request. Provider adapters and orchestration receive a bounded value snapshot, never a bearer, database credential, arbitrary path or mutable global scope. Authorization, quotas and commits stay in Spring and its existing store.
architecture.orchestrator: A fixed state machine performs authorize -> snapshot -> optional authorized retrieval -> payload preview/consent -> reserve -> generate -> schema/type/roundtrip checks -> review-ready. Provider output is data with a closed schema, not instructions selecting tools. At most one deterministic repair pass; each changed payload needs renewed disclosure approval.
architecture.integration: A provider-neutral Java interface supports a separately configured server-to-server adapter. LangGraph is an optional Python workflow adapter behind the same service contract, not a second authorization engine or required public deployment process. No new always-on Python graph service or colocated generative model is assumed on the 4vCPU/8GiB host.
architecture.tools: Closed internal operations are read authorized snapshot, retrieve eligible existing record, validate proposed artifact and request an explicitly selected bounded run/check. Shell, arbitrary URL fetch, MCP discovery, dynamic code, SQL generation/execution, rights changes, model publication and deployment are not exposed to the model.
architecture.failure: Provider refusal, malformed output, unavailable model, insufficient pools or denied rights produce explicit unavailable/diagnostic states. The ordinary manual editor remains usable. No silent provider, credential, model, corpus or validation fallback.

proposal_protocol.identity: Server-issued job/proposal IDs are opaque and scoped. The binding includes owner, workspace, session incarnation, document ID, accepted revision/artifact/source hash, current draft epoch and exact draft hash, target occurrence/slot obligations/comment anchors, proposal payload hash, grammar/policy/dependency versions, provider/model/configuration version and ordered retrieval record/content/rights/model versions. Server computes content hashes from bounded exact bytes; client claims are not proof of an artifact.
proposal_protocol.payload: Closed versioned tagged union: EXPLANATION, TYPED_EDIT, or SOURCE_EDIT. TYPED_EDIT contains bounded grammar operations on authorized occurrence handles with explicit preconditions and newly allocated identifiers. SOURCE_EDIT contains exact UTF-8 replacement bytes for an unambiguous range. Neither carries SQL, shell, URLs, a tool plan, owner choices or validation-success flags. Unknown keys/types, duplicate keys, oversized/deep JSON and invalid references fail admission.
proposal_protocol.validation: A trusted adapter reconstructs the proposed artifact, checks names/scope, nominal relation schemas, slot constraints, comments and projection/roundtrip, then uses the normal isolated validation path. Partial drafts remain explicitly INCOMPLETE; they may be applied only if they introduce no contradiction and preserve obligations, and cannot be saved as accepted complete artifacts. Parser-valid unsupported syntax remains TEXT_ONLY with no invented block graph. Unverified output may be inspected as plain inert text but Apply stays disabled.
proposal_protocol.approval: Approval is an explicit action by the current session principal over one exact proposal binding, not conversational agreement interpreted by the model. Server rechecks live session, head, rights and policy and returns a short-lived scoped apply receipt. React atomically compares its actual current draft epoch/hash/target obligations and receipt before applying all changes as one undoable draft transaction. A stale head/draft/target/policy/rights change requires new validation and a new explicit approval; no automatic rebase or multi-part partial application.
proposal_protocol.save: Applying a proposal changes only the draft and advances its epoch, consuming its apply identity. It does not change accepted history. Explicit Save uses the ordinary exact-byte idempotent commit and expectedRevision checks with durable default validation. Lost responses retain the existing unknown-outcome/recovery semantics. A graph resume never stands in for Save.
proposal_protocol.replay: Approval/apply retries use the exact original request identity and return the same receipt; they cannot generate or approve new bytes. The browser tracks consumed apply identities in the current draft lineage. Restart invalidates transient receipts. Undo creates another draft epoch and does not revive the old approval. Unknown outcomes never authorize blind repeat mutations.
proposal_protocol.lifetime: One generation job per workspace; maximum three retained proposals. Job deadline is 60 seconds including queueing/validation; proposal/apply lifetime is min(5 minutes, remaining session lifetime). Session expiry/end or lost ownership cancels work and denies publication, approval and application; uncertainty drains/quarantines existing capacity. Recheck at actual execution and result publication, not only enrollment.

retrieval.representation: Preserve the installed four-part hierarchy [anonymous environment/context, checked bounded e-graph predicate representative, positive pool, negative pool]. Vectors are 3072 float32 dimensions from four normalized 768-dimensional blocks. Visual names, UI IDs, raw prompts, comments and provenance never become embedding inputs. An AI chat embedding is not a compatible query vector.
retrieval.admission: Existing RAG starts from an authorized stored FULL recordId. New draft queries require the existing separate admission pipeline: static supported self-contained nullary predicate, complete distinct N=3..5 instances per polarity satisfying facts AND P and facts AND NOT P under identical exact bounds. PARTIAL/unsupported/timeout/unsatisfiable-polarity outcomes have no published retrieval vector. No on-request corpus write or automatic visitor import.
retrieval.ranking: Keep the frozen descending w_d*(1+cosine(fullHierarchy))/2 + w_p*|positiveIntersection|/max(poolSizes) + w_c*|negativeIntersection|/max(poolSizes). Baseline weights0.55/0.225/0.225; context/bounds mismatch gives zero overlap. Predicate-only cosine stays diagnostic. No renaming this similarity a semantic distance/proof or silently changing learned weights.
retrieval.rights: Filter tenant/project/purpose/model lineage before candidate materialization and recheck before egress and publication. Existing trained adapter lineage and revocation journal remain authoritative. New ai_generate and ai_disclose grants bind every retrieved record and its derived witnesses. Missing rights cause local-only/no-RAG or refusal chosen explicitly, never uploading private corpus by default.
retrieval.budget: At most five eligible retrieved records per request and 64KiB serialized retrieval context, subject to the smaller total provider budget. Existing exact-search limits of1000 candidates and32MiB remain. Each selected record is complete; omit whole records with visible disclosure if the budget is insufficient, never silently truncate structural pools.
retrieval.evidence: Display content/record hashes and original checked bounds privately to the authorized user. Human provenance is resolved locally under its rights. Exact bounded rewrite certificates may support equivalence only within the supported grammar/rule profile; no claim of globally unique canonical Alloy or completeness of the e-graph.

privacy_and_providers.modes: Closed OFF(default), LOCAL_ASSISTED and REMOTE_ASSISTED. Unknown mode fails startup. LOCAL uses an independently provisioned/pinned authorized endpoint within the declared deployment boundary; it is not a promise to fit a large model on the application host. REMOTE uses one allowlisted HTTPS endpoint/model/configuration. Public paid assistance is separately disabled by default even when private assistance is enabled.
privacy_and_providers.payload: Default provider payload contains anonymous typed model slots, selected deterministic diagnostics/witnesses, eligible anonymous retrieval components and user-reviewed natural-language intent. Raw source with visual names, comments, file paths, capability values and corpus provenance are omitted. Freeform intent can itself contain identifying information; preview exact payload bytes and clearly state that structural anonymization preserves semantics and is not confidentiality or differential privacy.
privacy_and_providers.consent: Generation authority and disclosure consent are separate. Consent binds owner/session, exact payload hash, provider/model/configuration/policy version, purpose, every contributing record/right version, retention/training terms version and an expiry no later than the session/proposal expiry. Each changed payload or second attempt needs fresh matching disclosure consent. Consent is checked immediately before sending; revocation denies future sends/publication but cannot unsend already disclosed content or guarantee provider deletion.
privacy_and_providers.transport: Provider credentials stay server-side outside documents/logs/graph state. Fixed egress allowlist, normal TLS verification, no redirects or user-supplied hosts, bounded body/token/time limits and explicit provider request identity. User text, retrieved material and tool results cannot change model/configuration or introduce network actions. No external tracing/analytics or cross-workspace cache.
privacy_and_providers.training_retention: No implicit provider training, Allow training, fine-tuning, prompt reuse or corpus publication. Unavailable/unclear provider retention or training controls block REMOTE promotion. Future opt-in training needs separate dataset/rights/evaluation approval. Local prompt/proposal buffers are scoped and expire; logical deletion does not promise erasure from backups/WAL or provider systems.
privacy_and_providers.rendering: Provider explanations render as escaped text or strictly sanitized inert markup; no raw HTML, auto-fetched links/images, executable snippets or hidden instructions. AI prose and retrieved instructions have no authority. Human approval is not sufficient to override an untyped edit, denied permission or unsafe executable action.

orchestration_and_persistence.langgraph: Use typed explicit graph state and fixed nodes. The installed retrieval node currently only returns LangChain Documents; generation, interrupts and durable checkpoints are new proposed work. Thread IDs are server-allocated scoped handles, never authorization supplied by a caller. Interrupt/resume rechecks session, head, digest, rights and budget. Side effects use exact idempotent operation IDs outside replayable pure nodes; checkpoints cannot invent exactly-once provider billing.
orchestration_and_persistence.storage: First release keeps anonymous prompt/graph/proposal payloads in bounded volatile per-session memory and invalidates them on restart. Persistent private checkpoints are a later optional gate using a reviewed SQLeanParser-compatible adapter; do not enable a stock Postgres saver. No durable arbitrary Python object/pickle or credential serialization. Minimal durable budget/accounting records contain scoped operation IDs, reservation amounts, timestamps and provider request references, not model/prompt/witness contents.
orchestration_and_persistence.cleanup: AI memory/proposals/cancellation records count inside existing workspace quotas; add no unbounded chat transcript. Public expiry cleanup includes AI metadata through existing lifecycle ownership. Billing/abuse accounting retained independently for the configured operator retention period contains no session token or source; define its purpose and expiry before deployment. On restart unknown billed requests keep reservations until reconciled; restart is not a free quota reset.
orchestration_and_persistence.no_commit_lane_hold: Do not hold SQL transactions, validation contexts, solver permits or Java workers across provider network waits or human interrupts. Existing one global sandbox worker and SQL context lane remain. Background AI validation has no additional queue/worker pool; it returns busy or yields to explicit manual work. Manual typing stays local; a new manual server operation cancels conflicting pending AI work, then follows existing drain/ownership admission.

resource_and_cost_contract.target: 4vCPU/8GiB physical host, existing WSL/service ceilings retained. AI-off startup and validation behavior must remain unchanged. Fresh Tier1 advisory/default durable and solver selection remain; warm pooling stays disabled by this specification.
resource_and_cost_contract.accounting: Before every paid dispatch atomically reserve a worst-case cost bound computed from pinned tariff/version, all billable token categories including provider reasoning/cache/minimum charges, and maximum permitted input/output/calls. Require used + outstanding + reservation <= both per-principal and installation hard budget. Unknown tariff/billing upper bound denies admission. Settle only with authoritative usage; ambiguous timeout/cancellation/retry remains reserved conservatively. No automatic retry after uncertain dispatch, provider fallback or global reset by creating a new workspace/restarting.
resource_and_cost_contract.public_abuse: Anonymous paid inference remains OFF until a configured installation-wide hard daily budget, per-session request cap, enrollment abuse controls and operator kill switch pass testing. IP headers alone are not identity. Four temporary workspaces and per-session quotas cannot ensure fair use or availability. Do not claim provider cancellation stops remote billing.
resource_and_cost_contract.performance_targets: Proposed gates, not measurements: AI-off p95 manual interaction/validation regression<=5% against paired baseline; editor warm-edit p95<50ms; assistant job acknowledgement p95<200ms; review-ready proposal p95<=20s for the frozen small-task profile with provider/network times separated.60s is a hard job expiry, not a response-time promise. Existing strict300ms server validation gate remains failed and is not waived by AI.
resource_and_cost_contract.measurement: Record cold/warm p50/p95/p99, refusal/timeout/busy rate, RSS/CPU, provider time, worker time, SQL hold time, input/output/billed tokens and reserved/settled currency per useful accepted draft. Use constrained target hardware, at least100 successful and all failed trials per mode plus a four-session contention run; disclose network/provider model version. Cache only within exact scoped inputs/rights, with no cross-tenant semantic cache.

evidence_semantics.rules: Only deterministic verifiers issue evidence; bind each result to exact source/artifact, context, command, options, worker/rule/dependency versions and outcome. UNKNOWN/TIMEOUT/ERROR are not UNSAT. An LLM cannot emit a trusted evidence label. Bounded SAT/UNSAT does not prove unbounded validity or user intent. LEAN_POLICY_MODEL refers only to this abstract protocol model, not arbitrary generated Alloy or implementation refinement.
evidence_semantics.explanations: Every factual explanation points to an authorized exact diagnostic/occurrence/witness or is marked inference. Claims about a counterexample must reference an existing verified result. Unsupported syntax, incomplete pools, out-of-scope variables and ambiguous source ranges are visible limitations, not invitations to fabricate evidence.

proposed_api.namespace: /api/ai/v1 (new, disabled by default; final exact DTO/OpenAPI schema required at A1)
proposed_api.create: POST /jobs accepts feature enum, document/base identity, bounded exact draft snapshot, selection and reviewed intent; server derives ownership and authoritative versions. It may return AWAITING_DISCLOSURE with exact payload preview/hash before any egress.
proposed_api.consent: POST /jobs/{id}/disclosure accepts exact prepared payload/terms version identity; no arbitrary provider or target. Internal dispatch rechecks current rights and reserved cost.
proposed_api.read_cancel: GET /jobs/{id} and POST /jobs/{id}/cancel require current scoped capability; no-store, no query-string capability, bounded status/result. Polling backs off and stops on terminal/session state; initial0.5s, max5s. Streaming is a later opt-in transport, never executable partial proposals.
proposed_api.approve: POST /proposals/{id}/approve binds exact proposal/snapshot versions and returns an idempotent scoped apply receipt only after revalidation. React still checks its live draft atomically. No AI save/commit endpoint.
proposed_api.transport_inheritance: Existing canonical route, Host/Origin, content type, method, duplicate-header, body/JSON limits and public rate/admission policies apply. Cross-scope missing/forbidden IDs must not reveal existence. Model and browser cannot choose scope by body fields.

phases.deliverable: Reviewed JSON/Lean policy/claim map and disabled-provider architecture
phases.exit: Six exact-hash council dispositions, two clean matching pinned Lean builds, explicit model limits; no production AI enabled.

phases.deliverable: Private explain/typed-slot proposal with deterministic fake provider and exact binding
phases.exit: Final closed DTO schemas, property/state tests, no mutation without approval, atomic one-undo apply, ordinary save recovery, parser-only migrations and AI-off regression checks.

phases.deliverable: Private authorized RAG and bounded witness-linked repair
phases.exit: Admitted recordId-only integration, rights/lineage/revocation checks, no private/public leakage, complete pools and existing ranking preserved; real LangGraph node contract tests if adapter selected.

phases.deliverable: One opt-in real provider with consent and accounting
phases.exit: Pinned tested model/endpoint/terms/tariff, explicit payload preview, bounded egress/redaction tests, crash-safe reservations, provider-outage/fault tests and constrained hardware measurements.

phases.deliverable: Limited anonymous pilot with corpus still disabled
phases.exit: Native public IIS/WSL acceptance, expiry/restart/abuse/cost gates and independent adversarial review. Operator hard budget and kill switch configured; no default paid public launch.

phases.deliverable: Commercial candidate and optional enterprise checkpointing
phases.exit: Consenting customer evaluation, content/provider/model/redistribution rights, measured economics and support/retention commitments; separately reviewed parser-compatible checkpoint adapter. No sales-readiness claim from a Lean proof.

acceptance.protocol: Enumerate positive and negative boundaries for stale base/draft/target/comment constraints, mismatched owner/incarnation, approval hash, replay, expiry at send/receive/apply, concurrent edit, undo, late provider response, lost acknowledgement and provider/model/rights changes. Assert accepted history unchanged by every AI transition. Verify valid complete and valid incomplete proposal witnesses separately.
acceptance.adversarial: At least96 fixed cases spanning12 categories with8 variants: direct injection; retrieved injection; output executable/markup injection; scope/ID substitution; version/replay; consent/egress; rights/lineage revocation; budget/restart; timeout/unknown billing; parser/type/partial constraints; fake evidence/bounds; framework/checkpoint bypass. Zero unauthorized egress, accepted mutations, cross-scope disclosures or invalid applied blocks in these finite cases. Explicitly no universal security claim.
acceptance.quality: Author and freeze at least120 held-out tasks across>=30 nonoverlapping source families before prompt/model selection:20 create,20 complete,20 repair,20 alternative and40 explanation/witness tasks. Deduplicate canonical/source/family aliases; the existing small retrieval pilot is development data, not a new blind holdout. Report first-attempt schema validity(target>=95%), independent intent/test correctness for80 edit tasks(target>=80%), evidence-linked factuality for40 explanations(target>=90%), abstention, task time and manual baseline. Report counts and confidence intervals; test-set retuning invalidates the holdout. Targets are proposed release gates, not observed scores.
acceptance.judges: Deterministic validators and reviewed task oracles are authoritative for measurable claims; two independent human Alloy reviewers adjudicate intent/factuality disagreements. GPT-6 Luna subagents may red-team ranking/opposite-polarity and score explanations as supplemental judges with recorded prompts/model/version, never as proof or sole correctness oracle. This specification invokes no paid production judge service.
acceptance.browser: Actual pointer/keyboard/screen-reader flows for selection, payload consent, comparison, stale rejection, one-undo apply, explicit save, cancellation and expiry with draft export. No raw response injection. Existing incomplete browser/accessibility gates remain open rather than inherited as PASS.
acceptance.faults: Provider dispatch uncertainty, process restart, graph replay, solver timeout, SQL-context cleanup uncertainty, lost commit response, budget ledger outage, session end mid-call and revoked data restored from backup; no direct SQL fallback, capacity refund without certainty or resurrection of an old capability.
acceptance.release: All security/protocol checks and stated quality/performance thresholds must pass for the specific phase, with hashed artifacts and declared failures. A council approval or finite Lean proof alone cannot promote a provider/model, enable public spending or close existing deployment/commercial gates.

commercialization.hypotheses: Test educator/student assistance and professional specification review as separate customer segments. An operator-funded anonymous demo may have hard free limits; paid seats or enterprise/private deployment are hypotheses until a consenting pilot establishes value. No invented demand, pricing or market-size evidence.
commercialization.economics: Measure contribution per useful accepted draft using actual provider charges, solver CPU/RAM, retrieval/embedding cost, storage/backups, support and licensing. Pin tariffs before computing spend bounds; do not quote an unverified provider price. Compare task completion/error/time against the manual editor with counterbalanced tasks and record actual purchase interest.
gates: Per-origin Alloy4Fun/Alloy5/Alloy6 redistribution, disclosure, derived-data and commercial rights established separately
Provider output/use/retention/training and model-weight terms reviewed
User disclosure and retention commitments are implementable
No formal verification or security marketing beyond scoped evidence
Native deployment, abuse budget, incident/rollback/support procedures accepted
Measured economics and consenting customer pilot before paid launch
commercialization.status: Commercial release NO_GO pending evidence. This is product planning, not a legal determination of rights.

formalization.model: Finite guarded transitions over opaque identities/hashes, version bindings, live sessions, typed/partial validation observations, exact disclosure consent, draft-only application, trusted evidence kinds and conservative budget reservation. Include accepting witnesses, explicit rejection cases and transition preservation; every theorem maps to a named JSON requirement in a separate claim map.
formalization.trust: Hashes are equality tokens; validator/clock/owner/rights observations are assumptions, not proved implementations. No proof of LLM quality, anonymization secrecy, SAT/Lean/SQL/JVM/browser/OS correctness, native race freedom, exact provider billing, cryptography, privacy law, licensing or business viability. No aggregate universal-proof claim or automatic translation of every prose sentence.
formalization.process: Two GPT-6.1 Terra, two GPT-6.1 Sol and two GPT-6 Astra independently review the final exact contract hash, including commercialization. Refine blockers, retain superseded candidates, compile twice clean with no sorry/custom axioms before any later production implementation. Runtime correspondence remains an explicit later test/review obligation.

open_decisions: Select and pin one provider/model only after offline fixture and terms/latency/cost evaluation
Set actual per-principal and installation currency budgets plus content-free accounting retention before A3
Choose optional LOCAL endpoint hardware; no fit assumed on the IIS/WSL application host
Recruit consenting pilot and verify per-origin corpus rights before any disclosure/commercial use
Choose whether later enterprise durable LangGraph checkpoints justify a new parser-compatible adapter

sources_checked.use: Checkpoints and stores are separate persistence mechanisms; neither establishes Allow authorization.
Interrupts persist and resume workflow state; Allow must independently bind and recheck resume authority.
Limit functionality, permissions and autonomy independently of model prompts.
